scene_objective: In the Setup phase, establish Ben Skywalker's private unease with a persistent wrongness in the Force by showing it cost him a sparring match in front of another Knight, planting the hook that something is disrupting his otherwise reliable perception and isolating him from the Order's dismissal of it as post-Abeloth residue.

turning_point.trigger: Running a form without igniting the blade in the empty salle, Ben feels the half-beat lag in the ambient field steal a timing he cannot compensate for.
turning_point.shift: The wrongness moves from a private cost he could rationalize as fatigue to an undeniable disruption he must confront rather than hide.
turning_point.cost: Ben loses the last of his self-assurance that he can manage this alone; the reluctant hope that Luke's arrival might offer an outlet wars with the fear that admitting it will brand him as unreliable or still traumatized.

closing_beat: Luke appeared in the doorway with a datapad and an expression Ben knew meant a mission.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben's guard drops a half-second late and his sparring partner's training blade catches him across the shoulder.
key_beats.state_change: The match ends with Ben scored on; the partner registers surprise at the uncharacteristic error.
key_beats.pov_reaction: A flush of irritation prickles under his collar; his fingers tighten on the hilt as the half-beat lag echoes again in his inner ear.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben deactivates his training saber and waves off a rematch, claiming fatigue.
key_beats.state_change: The partner accepts the excuse without pressing and leaves the salle, leaving Ben alone under the lights.
key_beats.pov_reaction: His shoulders settle into a heavier hunch; the excuse tastes like ash, sharpening the isolation he has been nursing all week.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben paces the empty salle alone, running through forms without igniting the blade to test whether the wrongness disrupts muscle memory or Force timing.
key_beats.state_change: The physical forms reveal the lag is deeper than muscle; the salle's ambient presence arrives consistently off-rhythm.
key_beats.pov_reaction: A cold tension coils low in his gut with each missed beat; his bare feet grip the floor harder as if anchoring himself against an invisible current.

key_beats.beat_description: Luke appears in the doorway with a datapad and mission-ready posture.
key_beats.state_change: An external demand arrives at the exact moment Ben has stopped pretending the problem is only fatigue.
key_beats.pov_reaction: A thin thread of reluctant hope flickers beneath the frustration; his pulse steadies even as the half-beat lag still thrums at the edge of awareness.

voice_guidance: Channel Zahn's efficient dialogue and tight third-person interiority — sharp, self-deprecating, never melodramatic. Interior voice stays raw and unfinished; sentences should feel like a man thinking on his feet rather than delivering analysis. Keep Force references sensory and vibrational, anchored to the single consistent half-beat lag metaphor. Surface dry wit in one self-directed jab at his own denial.
forbidden_moves: Do not allow any character outside Ben Skywalker and the unnamed Jedi Knight sparring partner to speak, act significantly, or interact.
Do not resolve or clinically name the nature of the wrongness; Ben feels it but does not articulate a structural diagnosis.
Do not import Disney-canon concepts; stay within Legends EU continuity.
Do not open a Force-perception passage with 'an ambient hum of…'.
Do not use visual or color terms to describe the wrongness.
anti_patterns: do not describe the wrongness in visual or color terms
keep it auditory and vibrational, and use one consistent metaphor for this scene (the half-beat lag in the ambient field)
he should not, in this scene, arrive at any clinical articulation of what the wrongness is
